page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-4 is an entry-tier compute-oriented instance configuration within the legacy N1 machine family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz using the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of approximately 0.9 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no bundled local storage, lacks dedicated GPU hardware, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate limited raw computational and memory throughput across standard workloads. Synthetic processor evaluation shows a Geekbench single-core score of 926.0 and multi-core score of 1979.0, both placing in the bottom 10 percent of recorded results. PassMark testing records a CPU score of 3374.03 and a memory score of 987.38. Data handling and compression workloads exhibit modest throughput, with single-threaded gzip compression at 18.99 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 7.16 GB/sec. Cache hierarchy consists of 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and a shared 45 MB L3 cache.

The instance delivers weak performance characteristics for operational services, showing 2.8 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 2.92 GB/sec. Small-scale language model inference processing on a 135M parameter model reaches 160.16 tokens/sec for prompt ingestion and 57.08 tokens/sec for token generation. Due to the limited 4.0 GB memory footprint, benchmarks for 7B and 70B parameter models could not be executed.

The core architectural tradeoff of the n1-highcpu-4 is its high vCPU count relative to its constrained memory capacity. With no local storage or modern AVX-512 vector support, it is economically tailored for lightweight, stateless tasks that require multithreading over memory density. It is functionally aligned with lightweight batch processing, small CI/CD build agents, basic static web serving, and low-footprint microservices.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-4 is a compute-skewed virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The instance is allocated 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 4.0 GB of RAM, yielding an asymmetrical ratio of 0.9 GB memory per core. The configuration lacks local storage, integrated GPUs, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic performance benchmarks reflect entry-level capabilities, with a single-core Geekbench score of 926.0, multi-core score of 1979.0, and PassMark CPU score of 3374.03. Memory-intensive tests similarly rank in the bottom quartiles, such as a PassMark memory score of 987.38 and large-block memory read bandwidth of 25.58 GB/sec. Given its constrained memory pool and lack of AVX-512 extensions, n1-highcpu-4 is primarily suited for lightweight multithreaded compute tasks, simple build runners, small-scale batch scripts, and modest web request processing.
